name: Sessions
description: Total visits. The denominator for most ratios.
action: A swing of 20% or more week on week: split by channel before doing anything else.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs or your own page-view beacon also count visitors who block or decline GA4. Filter out bots.

name: Users and new users
description: Unique reach, and how much of it is first contact.
action: Flat new users with rising sessions means growth is coming from repeat visits only.
first_party: First-party worksOwn first-party cookie or a daily-salted hash. Counting people across days needs a stored ID, which may need consent.

name: Sessions by channel group
description: Which channels carry the traffic.
action: One channel above half of all sessions is a concentration risk. Diversify.
first_party: First-party worksClassify the referrer and UTM tags on your own endpoint.

name: Source and medium
description: The exact origin of each visit.
action: Many sessions labelled (not set) or (other): fix tagging first.
first_party: Best first-partySave referrer and UTM on the first request and store them with the lead. It survives blockers.

name: Conversion rate by channel
description: Channel quality, not just quantity.
measure: GA4 key events divided by sessions, per channel
action: Move budget and effort to channels that beat the site average.
first_party: Best first-partyJoin stored source to your own lead and order records. No sampling, no consent gap on the conversion side.

name: Landing page sessions
description: Which pages open the visit.
action: Top landing pages with weak engagement are the cheapest fixes.
first_party: First-party worksServer logs or beacon, first page of each visit.

name: New versus returning visitors
description: Discovery against loyalty.
action: Returning share falling while the site depends on repeat sales: add email capture.
first_party: First-party worksFirst-party cookie. Browsers shorten script-set cookies, so returning visitors are understated.

name: Referring sites
description: Which outside sites send people and what those people do.
action: A referrer with high engagement: ask for more placements, or a partnership.
first_party: First-party worksThe Referer header in your logs.

name: Geography and city
description: Whether visitors are inside the area you serve.
action: Large traffic from places you do not serve: exclude them from ads and reports.
first_party: First-party worksLook up the IP at request time and discard it. Do not store raw IPs.

name: Device, browser and OS split
description: What people use, so you test on it.
action: Any browser above 5% of traffic with a lower conversion rate gets tested first.
first_party: First-party worksParse the user agent on the server.

name: Cost per session (paid)
description: What a visit costs by campaign.
action: Rising cost with flat conversion rate: pause or rewrite the campaign.
first_party: First-party worksYour own session count divided by ad spend you enter or import.

name: Seasonality index
description: Expected high and low months for your business.
measure: This month compared with the same month last year
action: Compare year on year, never month on month, in a seasonal business.
first_party: First-party worksYour own history, kept past any tool's retention limit.

name: Day of week and hour
description: When visitors arrive and when they convert.
measure: GA4 Explore, hour and day dimensions
action: Schedule posts, emails, ads and staff cover around the conversion peaks.
first_party: First-party worksEvent timestamps.

name: Branded search trend
description: Brand demand, a proxy for word of mouth and offline reach.
measure: Search Console queries containing your name, plus Google Trends
action: Falling branded searches signal weakening awareness before revenue shows it.
first_party: Not first-partySearch queries are held by Google. You only see the click, not the query.

name: Share of voice
description: Your rank-weighted search visibility against named rivals.
measure: SEO tool, tracked keyword set, three competitors
action: Rivals gaining on your core topics: prioritise those topic clusters.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds rank data from search results, which only rank trackers hold.

name: Dark social proxy
description: Shares in chats and email apps, which arrive as Direct.
measure: GA4 Direct sessions landing on deep URLs, not the homepage
action: High deep-URL direct traffic: add share buttons and trackable short links.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs show deep-URL arrivals with no referrer, with no tag needed.

name: Traffic from AI assistants
description: Whether chat and answer engines send visitors, and to which pages.
measure: GA4 source filter for chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com and similar
action: Strengthen the pages being cited; add clear answers and structured data.
first_party: First-party worksReferrer header and user agent in logs. Some assistants send neither. Logs also show AI crawler visits.

name: UTM coverage
description: Share of campaign visits carrying a campaign tag.
measure: GA4 sessions where campaign is (not set), from email, ads and social
action: Below full coverage, channel reports mislead. Enforce one naming sheet.
first_party: First-party worksYour endpoint can flag landing requests that arrive without tags.

name: Engagement rate
description: Share of sessions that were engaged (the 10 second, key event or 2 page view test).
action: Landing pages under the site average: fix headline, intent match and speed.
first_party: First-party worksYour own timer, scroll and click events. Copy GA4's rule (10 seconds, key event, 2 views) to stay comparable.

name: Bounce rate (GA4)
description: The inverse of engagement rate. Not the old Universal Analytics number.
action: Use it only as the flip side of engagement. Do not compare with old reports.
first_party: First-party worksInvert your own engagement rate. Do not build a second definition.

name: Average engagement time
description: Foreground time with the page active, not idle tabs.
action: Short time on an answer page can be good. Read it with conversions.
first_party: First-party worksPage Visibility heartbeat from your script. Accuracy depends on that script.

name: Pages per session
description: Depth of exploration.
action: Low on a site built for browsing: improve related links and navigation.
first_party: First-party worksCount page requests per visit.

name: Scroll depth
description: Whether readers reach your call to action.
measure: GA4 enhanced measurement fires at 90%. Add 25, 50, 75 as custom events
action: If most readers stop at 50%, move the call to action above that line.
first_party: First-party worksA small own script posts 25, 50, 75, 90.

name: Key page click-through
description: Share of visitors who click the main call to action.
measure: GA4 click events on the button, divided by page views
action: Under your own baseline: test copy, colour contrast, position.
first_party: First-party worksClick listener posting to your endpoint.

name: Exit rate by page
description: Where visits end.
measure: GA4 Explore, exits divided by views
action: Exits on pages that are not goal pages are leaks. Add a next step.
first_party: First-party worksLast page of each visit.

name: Internal search usage
description: Share of sessions that use site search.
action: High usage means navigation fails. Rework menus and category pages.
first_party: Best first-partyYour server sees every search directly, with no tag to maintain.

name: Top internal search terms
description: Live demand in the visitors' own words.
action: Terms with no matching page become new pages or products.
first_party: Best first-partyLogged by your own search code, in full.

name: Zero-result search rate
description: Searches that return nothing.
measure: Site search logs or GA4 custom event
action: Every top zero-result term: add content, a synonym or a redirect.
first_party: Best first-partyOnly your server knows how many results it returned. Third-party tools never see this without custom code.

name: Search exit rate
description: Visitors who search and then leave.
action: High rate: the results page is not answering. Fix ranking of results.
first_party: First-party worksLast event of a visit is a search.

name: Rage clicks
description: Repeated fast clicks on one spot: broken or misleading elements.
action: Cluster on one element: fix it before sending more traffic.
first_party: Possible, not advisedClick-cluster detection is a few dozen lines, but replay is costly to build. Use a replay tool.

name: Dead clicks
description: Clicks that do nothing, often on things that look like buttons.
action: Make it a link or remove the styling that suggests it is one.
first_party: Possible, not advisedNeeds element-level event capture and upkeep. Use a replay tool.

name: Quick backs
description: Visitor lands, then hits back within seconds.
action: Message mismatch with the ad or search result. Rewrite the page top.
first_party: Possible, not advisedBack navigation is hard to detect reliably. Use a replay tool.

name: Excessive scrolling
description: Fast up-and-down scrolling that signals searching, not reading.
action: Add a summary, anchors or a table of contents near the top.
first_party: Possible, not advisedNeeds replay-grade capture. Use a replay tool.

name: Copy events
description: Visitors copying a phone number, email or address.
action: A copy is intent. Make that detail a tap-to-call or mailto link.
first_party: First-party worksCopy listener posting to your endpoint. Do not capture the copied text.

name: Tap-to-call, email and directions clicks
description: Direct contact intent, vital for local and service sites.
measure: GA4 click events on tel:, mailto: and map links
action: Treat each as a conversion. Track by page and campaign.
first_party: First-party worksClick listener on tel:, mailto: and map links. It shows intent, not a connected call.

name: Video plays and completion
description: Whether video earns attention.
measure: GA4 video events or the host's analytics
action: Drop-off at one point: cut or re-edit that moment.
first_party: First-party worksPlayer events posted from your page. Video hosts report their own plays too.

name: File downloads and outbound clicks
description: Interest in assets, and where you send people away.
action: High downloads: gate or follow up. High outbound: check you are not leaking buyers.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs record every download, including direct links from other sites. Outbound clicks need a listener.

name: Heatmap click distribution
description: Where attention and clicks cluster on a page.
action: Most clicks go to non-links: relocate the real call to action.
first_party: Possible, not advisedYou can log x and y clicks, but drawing heatmaps on responsive layouts is costly. Use a tool.

name: Returning visitor frequency
description: How often and how recently people come back.
measure: GA4 Explore, cohort or user lifetime
action: Long gaps: use email or reminders to bring them back.
first_party: First-party worksFirst-party ID. Limited by cookie lifespan.

name: Time to first interaction
description: How soon a visitor clicks, taps or scrolls.
measure: Custom event timestamp, or RUM tooling
action: Slow first interaction on mobile: a layout or speed problem.
first_party: Best first-partyYour script can timestamp the first interaction, which few tools expose.

name: Conversion rate
description: Share of sessions that reach a key event.
measure: GA4 key events divided by sessions
action: Track by channel, device and landing page. Test the weakest large segment.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own lead and order records are the source of truth. Only the session count can be undercounted.

name: Key event volume
description: Absolute count of the actions that matter.
action: Falling count with steady traffic: check tracking and form delivery first.
first_party: Best first-partyYour database counts every submission, including from visitors who block analytics.

name: Lead volume
description: Enquiries received.
measure: CRM or form tool, matched to GA4
action: Compare to form events. A gap means leads are being lost.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own lead store. Store the lead before sending any email so nothing is lost.

name: Cost per lead
description: What an enquiry costs.
action: Rising: look at ad quality, landing page and tracking before cutting spend.
first_party: First-party worksOwn lead count divided by spend you record.

name: Customer acquisition cost (CAC)
description: Full cost to win a customer.
measure: Sales and marketing spend divided by new customers
action: Above your margin-based limit: fix the weakest channel or the close rate.
first_party: First-party worksBilling and CRM records are first-party data.

name: Return on ad spend (ROAS)
description: Revenue per advertising dollar.
measure: Ad revenue divided by ad spend
action: Use profit on ad spend where margins differ by product.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own order revenue is the honest numerator. Ad platforms grade their own work.

name: Marketing efficiency ratio
description: Total revenue divided by total marketing spend. Immune to attribution fights.
action: Falling while channel ROAS looks fine: attribution is flattering something.
first_party: First-party worksFinance and order data, not analytics.

name: Revenue
description: Money in, by source.
action: Reconcile monthly with the payment processor. They should match closely.
first_party: Best first-partyYour order and payment records. Reconcile analytics to them.

name: Average order value
description: Spend per order.
action: Low: test bundles, thresholds for free shipping, add-ons.
first_party: First-party worksOrder records.

name: Revenue per session
description: Revenue divided by sessions. Combines conversion rate and order value.
measure: GA4 Monetization, or revenue divided by sessions
action: Best single number for judging a test or a page change.
first_party: First-party worksOwn orders divided by own session count.

name: Add-to-cart rate
description: Interest turning into intent.
measure: GA4 add_to_cart divided by product views
action: Low: improve photos, price clarity, reviews on the product page.
first_party: First-party worksCart events logged server-side.

name: Cart abandonment rate
description: Shoppers who start and do not finish. The Baymard average across 50 studies is 70.22%.
action: Top reason there is extra costs (40%). Show total cost early and offer guest checkout.
first_party: Best first-partyA carts table with created and completed states, including visitors who declined analytics.

name: Checkout step drop-off
description: The exact step where buyers quit.
action: Fix the largest single drop first: shipping, account wall, payment.
first_party: First-party worksLog each step on the server.

name: Payment failure rate
description: Declined or errored payments.
action: High rate: add wallets, check card verification settings, test on mobile.
first_party: First-party worksProcessor webhooks into your own database. The processor dashboard stays the primary source.

name: Form completion rate
description: Starts that become submissions.
action: Below your baseline: shorten the form, fix errors, add reassurance.
first_party: First-party worksSubmits are logged server-side. Starts need a small client script.

name: Form field drop-off
description: Which field makes people quit.
action: Remove or make optional the field with the largest exit.
first_party: Possible, not advisedPossible with focus and blur events, but risks capturing typed text and costs upkeep. Use a form tool.

name: Form error rate
description: Validation errors per submission attempt.
action: Frequent errors on one field: loosen the rule or clarify the format.
first_party: Best first-partyYour server-side validation already knows every error. Log it.

name: Micro-conversions
description: Early signals: pricing view, newsletter signup, video watched.
action: Use them when macro conversions are too rare to measure within weeks.
first_party: First-party worksCustom events to your own endpoint.

name: Funnel conversion by step
description: Every stage from landing to goal.
action: Fix steps in order of drop-off volume, not order of the funnel.
first_party: First-party worksOwn event table and a SQL query, or a self-hosted tool.

name: Lead to qualified rate
description: Share of leads sales accepts.
measure: CRM stages by source and landing page
action: Channels with many leads but few qualified: change targeting or form questions.
first_party: Best first-partyCRM stages only you hold.

name: Lead to customer rate
description: True lead quality, by source.
measure: CRM, source captured on the form
action: Judge channels by customers, not leads.
first_party: Best first-partyYour CRM joined to stored source. No third-party tool has this.

name: Speed to lead
description: Time from form submission to the first human reply.
measure: CRM timestamps, or form tool plus inbox
action: Set an alert. Slow replies lose leads that cost money to acquire.
first_party: Best first-partyOnly your own timestamps (submitted, first reply) can measure it.

name: Call answer rate and missed calls
description: Whether paid-for calls reach a person.
action: Missed calls in business hours: route to staff or a text-back.
first_party: Not first-partyPhone data lives with the provider. Import it if they offer webhooks.

name: Calls longer than 60 seconds
description: Calls that were real conversations.
action: Use as the call conversion in ads, not raw call count.
first_party: Not first-partyCall length lives with the call-tracking provider. Import it if possible.

name: Sales cycle length
description: Days from first touch to close.
action: Lengthening cycle: add proof, pricing clarity or follow-up content.
first_party: Best first-partyCRM timestamps.

name: Sessions to convert
description: Visits per customer before they act.
action: Many touches: invest in retargeting, email and remarketing content.
first_party: First-party worksNeeds a stored visitor ID across visits. Cookie lifespan and consent limit it.

name: Assisted conversions
description: Channels that help but do not close.
action: Do not cut channels that assist heavily just because they close little.
first_party: Possible, not advisedFirst and last touch are easy. A full multi-touch model is costly and easy to get wrong.

name: Pricing page to conversion
description: Intent from visitors who looked at price.
measure: GA4 funnel, pricing page as step one
action: Low: price presentation, plan clarity, or missing proof.
first_party: First-party worksPage view event then conversion for the same visitor.

name: Booking or demo show rate
description: Booked appointments that actually happen.
action: Low show rate: add reminders, shorten the lead time.
first_party: Best first-partyYour bookings table with attendance marked.

name: Customer lifetime value
description: Total margin per customer over time.
action: Set CAC limits from this, not from first-order revenue.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own order and billing history.

name: Lifetime value to CAC ratio
description: Whether growth pays for itself.
action: Low ratio: improve retention or cut acquisition cost before scaling spend.
first_party: Best first-partyBoth inputs come from your own records.

name: CAC payback period
description: Months to earn back acquisition cost.
measure: CAC divided by monthly margin per customer
action: Long payback strains cash. Raise prices, upsell or lower CAC.
first_party: First-party worksBilling and spend records.

name: Repeat purchase rate
description: Customers who buy again.
action: Low: build post-purchase email and reorder prompts.
first_party: Best first-partyOrders grouped by customer in your own database.

name: Refund and return rate
description: Fit between promise and product.
action: High on one product: fix the page description or the product.
first_party: Best first-partyYour order system.

name: Coupon code usage
description: Discount dependence, and leaks to coupon sites.
action: Many empty-field coupon searches: hide the code box or offer an on-page code.
first_party: Best first-partyYour order system records each code used.

name: Revenue per page
description: Which pages earn, including content that assists.
measure: GA4 page value or attributed conversions
action: Put internal links to top earners on high-traffic pages.
first_party: First-party worksRevenue by stored landing page works. Splitting credit across a whole path is a model: not advised.

name: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
description: How fast the main content appears. Good: 2.5 seconds or less.
measure: PageSpeed Insights, Search Console Core Web Vitals report
action: Over 2.5 s: compress the hero image, preload it, fix server response.
first_party: First-party worksGoogle's open-source web-vitals library can send your own real-user data. Browser support varies.

name: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
description: How fast the page responds to taps and clicks. Good: 200 ms or less.
action: Over 200 ms: cut long JavaScript tasks and heavy third-party scripts.
first_party: First-party worksSame library. Covers pages too small to appear in Google's report.

name: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
description: Visual stability. Good: 0.1 or less.
action: Over 0.1: set image sizes, reserve space for embeds and banners.
first_party: First-party worksSame library.

name: Share of URLs passing Core Web Vitals
description: Site-wide pass rate, mobile and desktop.
measure: Search Console Core Web Vitals report
action: Fix the largest group of similar failing URLs first (one template fixes many).
first_party: First-party worksCompute it from your own real-user data per URL. Search Console gives Google's view.

name: Time to First Byte (TTFB)
description: Server response time. A diagnostic for slow LCP.
action: High TTFB: caching, a CDN, database or hosting tier.
first_party: Best first-partyServer timing in your own logs is exact.

name: First Contentful Paint (FCP)
description: First visible paint. A diagnostic for render-blocking resources.
action: Late FCP: inline critical CSS, defer scripts and fonts.
first_party: First-party worksReal-user library.

name: Total Blocking Time (TBT)
description: Lab proxy for responsiveness.
action: High TBT: split bundles, remove unused scripts.
first_party: Not first-partyA lab-only metric. Run Lighthouse in your build pipeline.

name: Mobile versus desktop gap
description: Where the experience is worse.
measure: Core Web Vitals report split by device
action: Mobile much worse: test on a mid-range phone and throttled network.
first_party: First-party worksSplit your own real-user data by device.

name: Page weight and request count
description: Bytes and files per page.
action: Heavy pages: modern image formats, lazy-load below the fold, drop unused libraries.
first_party: First-party worksBuild output and the browser's Resource Timing.

name: JavaScript bundle size
description: The cost of code shipped to every visitor.
action: Growing release by release: set a budget and fail builds that exceed it.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own build already knows. Fail builds over budget.

name: Third-party script cost
description: Time added by chat, ads, tags and widgets.
action: Remove any tag nobody reads. Load the rest after interaction.
first_party: First-party worksResource Timing in your real-user data. Lighthouse is easier for a one-off.

name: Field versus lab gap
description: Whether tests reflect real users.
action: Large gap: your audience has slower devices or networks than your tests.
first_party: First-party worksYour real-user data against your pipeline's Lighthouse.

name: Uptime
description: Share of time the site is reachable.
action: Any outage: alert the owner and write down cause and fix.
first_party: Possible, not advisedA monitor on the same server cannot see its own outage. Use an outside monitor.

name: Server error rate (5xx)
description: Requests failing on your side.
action: Rising: check recent deploys before anything else.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs record every failure, including ones no browser script can report.

name: Mean time to recovery
description: How fast you fix outages.
action: Long recovery: add automatic rollback and clearer alerts.
first_party: First-party worksYour own incident log.

name: JavaScript errors per 1,000 sessions
description: Hidden breakage in real browsers.
action: One error on the checkout or form path outranks everything else.
first_party: First-party worksError handler posting to your endpoint. Hosted error tools are easier.

name: Synthetic check pass rate
description: Scripted run of contact form, search, checkout every few minutes.
action: A failed check on a revenue path: treat as an outage.
first_party: Possible, not advisedPossible with a scheduled job, but running it inside your own infrastructure shares its failure.

name: CDN cache hit ratio
description: Share of requests served without hitting your server.
action: Low ratio: fix cache headers, long-cache static assets.
first_party: Best first-partyCDN and origin logs.

name: Server latency at p95
description: What the slowest 5% of requests experience.
action: p95 far above the median: look for slow queries and cold starts.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own application timing.

name: Lighthouse score
description: A single lab run, easy to game and noisy.
action: Use it to find issues. Do not report it as a KPI.
first_party: First-party worksRuns in your own build pipeline. Still a lab score.

name: Organic clicks
description: Visits earned from Google.
action: Compare 28 days against the previous period and the same period last year.
first_party: First-party worksCount visits with a search-engine referrer. This sees clicks, not queries. Search Console stays the query source.

name: Impressions
description: Visibility, before the click.
action: Rising impressions with flat clicks is a title or snippet problem.
first_party: Not first-partyOnly Google knows how often you appeared.

name: Click-through rate
description: How often an appearance becomes a visit.
action: Pages with high impressions and low CTR: rewrite title and description.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds impressions, which only Google holds.

name: Average position
description: Typical ranking. An average that hides spread.
measure: Search Console, by query or page
action: Judge by page and query, never only sitewide.
first_party: Not first-partyOnly Google or a rank tracker knows your rank.

name: Striking-distance queries
description: Queries ranking roughly 8 to 20 with real impressions. The cheapest gains.
action: Add internal links, expand the page, and improve the title for these first.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds query and position data from Search Console.

name: Branded versus non-branded clicks
description: Whether search finds strangers or only people who know you.
measure: Search Console, query filter on your name
action: Non-branded share small: build topic content for the problems you solve.
first_party: Not first-partySearch engines no longer pass the query. Use Search Console.

name: Queries per page
description: How many searches each page earns.
action: Page ranks for a few terms only: widen coverage of related questions.
first_party: Not first-partyQuery data lives in Search Console.

name: Top-3 and top-10 keyword count
description: Breadth of strong rankings.
action: Watch the trend of the count, not single keywords (results are personalised).
first_party: Possible, not advisedPossible by scraping results, but it breaks Google's terms and gets blocked. Use Search Console or a tracker.

name: Organic landing page conversions
description: Which search pages earn leads and sales.
measure: GA4 organic channel, landing page, key events
action: Pages with traffic but no conversions need an offer; pages with conversions need more links.
first_party: Best first-partyStored landing page and referrer joined to your own leads.

name: Indexed versus submitted pages
description: Whether Google keeps the pages you want.
action: Important pages excluded: fix noindex, canonical, thin content or crawl access.
first_party: Not first-partyIndex state is Google's. Your sitemap only tells you what you submitted.

name: Crawled, not indexed
description: Pages Google saw and passed over.
action: Large and growing: consolidate thin pages, improve quality or internal links.
first_party: Not first-partyOnly Search Console reports this.

name: Crawl stats
description: Crawl requests, response time and host problems.
action: Response times rising or errors spiking: investigate hosting first.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs show every Googlebot request. Search Console only summarises.

name: Sitemap coverage
description: Share of sitemap URLs indexed.
action: Low coverage: remove junk URLs from the sitemap.
first_party: Not first-partyYou know what you submitted, not what Google indexed.

name: Referring domains
description: Unique sites linking to you.
action: Prefer relevant links from real sites. Count of domains beats count of links.
first_party: Not first-partyLinks on other sites. Your logs only show links that sent a visit.

name: New and lost links
description: Link velocity and decay.
action: Lost link from a strong site: ask to restore it.
first_party: Not first-partyOther sites' pages. Needs a backlink tool.

name: Anchor text mix
description: Whether links look natural.
action: Heavy exact-match anchors: stop building that kind.
first_party: Not first-partyOther sites' pages. Needs a backlink tool.

name: Orphan pages and click depth
description: Pages with no internal links and pages buried 4 or more clicks deep.
action: Link important pages from high-traffic pages, within 3 clicks of home.
first_party: First-party worksCrawl your own site and compare to your own page list from the CMS.

name: Broken links and redirect chains
description: Wasted crawl and lost link value.
action: Fix internal broken links, and point redirects straight to the final URL.
first_party: First-party worksOwn crawl plus 404 logs.

name: Duplicate titles and descriptions
description: Pages that cannot be told apart.
action: Rewrite duplicates, starting with pages that earn impressions.
first_party: First-party worksOwn crawl or a build-time check.

name: Keyword cannibalization
description: Two of your pages competing for one query.
action: Merge pages, or differentiate their intent and cross-link.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds query data per page.

name: Structured data validity
description: Whether markup passes and shows rich results.
measure: Search Console Enhancements, Rich Results Test
action: Errors on a template: fix once, many pages recover.
first_party: First-party worksValidate markup in your build. Google's report shows what Google saw.

name: SERP feature ownership
description: Featured snippets, people-also-ask, local pack.
action: A snippet owned by a rival: restructure the answer in 40 to 60 words with a clear heading.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds result-page data.

name: Zero-click share
description: Queries answered without any click.
measure: Rank tracker or Search Console CTR by query type
action: Do not chase clicks on queries that never click. Target decisions.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds result-page data.

name: Content decay
description: Pages losing clicks year on year.
measure: Search Console, compare periods by page
action: Refresh the top decaying pages: update facts, add sections, relink.
first_party: First-party worksYour own search-referred visits per page over time.

name: Citations in AI answers
description: Whether answer engines name you.
measure: Manual checks of target questions, or a visibility tool
action: Absent: add clear definitions, data, authorship and schema to key pages.
first_party: Not first-partyThe answers live on the assistant's side. Check manually or with a tool.

name: Google Business Profile views, calls and directions
description: Local demand actions.
action: Low calls for views: fix category, hours, photos, phone number.
first_party: Not first-partyHeld by Google.

name: Review count, rating and velocity
description: Local trust and ranking signal.
action: Slow velocity: ask every happy customer. Reply to all reviews.
first_party: Not first-partyHeld by review platforms.

name: Review response rate
description: Whether you engage.
action: Reply within a few days. Aim for every review.
first_party: Not first-partyHeld by review platforms.

name: Name, address, phone consistency
description: Match across directories.
measure: Listing audit tool or manual check
action: Fix mismatches on the major directories first.
first_party: Not first-partyYour master record is first-party, but the comparison needs outside directories.

name: Local ranking grid
description: Rank by neighbourhood around the business.
action: Weak zones: add location content and reviews from those areas.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds location-specific result data.

name: Rank volatility
description: Whether movement is you or a Google update.
action: Wide volatility on a known update date: wait before changing anything.
first_party: Not first-partyNeeds many keywords tracked across sites.

name: Conversions assisted by content
description: Revenue and leads touched by articles and guides.
measure: GA4 conversion paths, landing page then key event
action: Double down on the topics that appear in winning paths.
first_party: First-party worksStored touches per visitor, if you keep them.

name: Organic entrances per piece
description: Search traffic per article.
action: Pieces with none after 6 months: improve, merge or remove.
first_party: First-party worksSearch-referred first pages by URL.

name: Read completion
description: Readers who reach the end.
action: Low completion on long pieces: add summary, tighter intro, subheads.
first_party: First-party worksScroll plus time events.

name: Newsletter signups per piece
description: Content that builds the list.
measure: GA4 event with page as dimension
action: Place signup prompts in the best performers.
first_party: Best first-partyThe signup record stores the page it came from.

name: Backlinks earned per piece
description: Content that others cite.
action: Repeat the formats that earn links: data, tools, original research.
first_party: Not first-partyLinks on other sites.

name: Time to first ranking
description: How long a new page takes to appear.
action: Slow: improve internal links to new pages, publish with a plan for links.
first_party: First-party worksProxy only: date of the first search-referred visit.

name: Topic cluster coverage
description: Share of the questions in your topic that you answer.
action: Gaps in the cluster: write the missing pages that link to the hub.
first_party: First-party worksYour content inventory against a topic list.

name: Content refresh rate
description: How much of the top content is updated yearly.
action: Top 20 pages unchanged for a year: schedule updates.
first_party: Best first-partyCMS last-modified dates. Nobody else has them.

name: Reader return within 30 days
description: Whether content builds habit.
action: Low: add related reading and email follow-up.
first_party: First-party worksFirst-party ID. Cookie lifespan limits it.

name: Social shares and saves
description: Resonance. A weak substitute for outcomes.
action: Use as a tie-breaker, not a goal.
first_party: Not first-partyHeld by the platforms.

name: Cost per piece and content ROI
description: Return on production spend.
action: Stop formats that never return their cost.
first_party: First-party worksYour costs against your own conversions.

name: Activation rate
description: New sign-ups who reach the first valuable action.
measure: Product events as a share of sign-ups
action: Low activation: cut steps and add a guided first task.
first_party: Best first-partyProduct events in your own database.

name: Time to value
description: How long until a user gets a result.
measure: Median time from sign-up to key action
action: Long time: remove setup, add templates and defaults.
first_party: Best first-partyTimestamps in your own database.

name: Cohort retention curve
description: Share of each sign-up month still active over time.
measure: Cohort analysis in GA4 or product analytics
action: Curve that never flattens means a leak. Fix onboarding before acquisition.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own user and event tables.

name: Churn rate
description: Customers or revenue lost per period.
action: Rising churn: interview leavers and review the first 30 days.
first_party: Best first-partyBilling records.

name: Net revenue retention
description: Revenue from existing customers after upgrades and losses.
action: Under 100%: the base shrinks even with new sales.
first_party: Best first-partyBilling records.

name: Active users and stickiness
description: Daily over monthly active users.
action: Low stickiness: build reasons to return, not more features.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own event tables.

name: Feature adoption
description: Share of users using each feature.
action: Unused features: remove or promote. Heavily used ones: invest.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own product events.

name: Account sign-up completion
description: Registrations started that finish.
action: Drop at verification: check email delivery and form length.
first_party: Best first-partyServer-side registration events.

name: Login failure rate
description: Users who cannot get in.
action: High rate: improve reset flow, add passwordless sign-in.
first_party: Best first-partyYour authentication logs.

name: Net Promoter Score
description: Willingness to recommend. Read the comments, not just the score.
action: Follow up with detractors within two days.
first_party: First-party worksYour own survey form, or a survey tool.

name: Customer satisfaction and effort scores
description: Satisfaction and ease after a specific interaction.
action: Low effort scores point to the exact process to simplify.
first_party: First-party worksYour own post-interaction survey.

name: Support tickets per 1,000 sessions
description: Friction the pages do not explain.
action: Cluster of tickets on one topic: fix the page or flow that causes it.
first_party: First-party worksHelpdesk export divided by your own sessions.

name: Help-doc deflection
description: Help views that do not become tickets.
action: Low deflection: rewrite the top articles in plain steps.
first_party: First-party worksYour docs views set against tickets.

name: Reactivation rate
description: Lapsed customers who return.
action: Time win-back email to the usual lapse point.
first_party: Best first-partyCRM and billing.

name: Referral and share rate
description: Customers who bring others.
action: Low: simplify the ask and reward both sides.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own referral codes and links.

name: Email click-through rate
description: Subscribers who clicked.
action: Test subject, offer and link position. Open rate is not a reliable substitute.
first_party: First-party worksClick-redirect links through your own domain. The email platform also reports it.

name: Click-to-open rate
description: Content quality among those who opened.
action: Low rate with healthy opens: the content or call to action misses.
first_party: Possible, not advisedDepends on open tracking, which privacy features distort.

name: Open rate
description: Distorted by mail privacy features that pre-load images.
action: Use only to compare sends under the same conditions.
first_party: Possible, not advisedA tracking pixel is possible but unreliable. Do not build it.

name: Net list growth
description: New subscribers less unsubscribes and bounces.
action: Shrinking list: add on-site capture and a welcome series.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own subscriber database.

name: Revenue per email
description: Money earned by each send.
action: Send more of what earns and less of what only gets opened.
first_party: First-party worksTagged links joined to your own orders.

name: Unsubscribe and spam complaint rate
description: Fatigue and relevance.
action: Complaints trending up: segment, slow down, tighten promises.
first_party: First-party worksUnsubscribes are yours. Complaint data partly comes from mailbox providers.

name: Deliverability and authentication
description: SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass rates and inbox placement.
action: Failures: fix DNS records. Poor reputation caps all email results.
first_party: First-party worksDMARC reports arrive at your own address. Parse them or use a free tool.

name: Cost per click and click-through rate (ads)
description: Auction cost and ad appeal.
action: Low CTR: test messages. High CPC: improve relevance and landing page.
first_party: Not first-partyAd platform data.

name: Impression share lost to budget and rank
description: Demand you missed on search ads.
action: Lost to budget with strong ROAS: add budget. Lost to rank: improve quality.
first_party: Not first-partyAd platform data.

name: Wasted spend on irrelevant queries
description: Share of ad spend on terms that cannot buy.
action: Add negatives weekly until waste is small.
first_party: Not first-partyThe search terms report lives with the ad platform.

name: Creative fatigue
description: Declining CTR with rising frequency.
measure: Ad platform, frequency and CTR trends
action: Refresh creative when CTR falls while frequency climbs.
first_party: Not first-partyAd platform data.

name: Landing page conversion by ad group
description: Whether the page keeps the promise of the ad.
action: Low conversion on a high-spend group: match page headline to the ad.
first_party: Best first-partyTagged landing visits joined to your own leads, free of platform self-attribution.

name: Social referral conversion
description: Value of a social visit.
action: Social that does not convert may still assist. Check paths first.
first_party: First-party worksReferrer and UTM against your own conversions.

name: Followers and impressions
description: Reach. A vanity metric unless tied to clicks.
action: Track clicks to site and saves. Ignore follower counts as a goal.
first_party: Not first-partyHeld by the platforms.

name: Form delivery check
description: Whether every submission reaches the inbox or CRM.
measure: Compare GA4 form_submit with CRM entries monthly, plus a test submission weekly
action: A gap means lost leads. Fix before spending more on traffic.
first_party: Best first-partyOnly possible with your own records: compare stored submissions with delivered email and CRM entries.

name: Tracking health
description: Whether analytics events still fire after releases.
measure: Test key events after every deploy, tag assistant, backend counts
action: Sudden drop in key events at a deploy time: tracking broke.
first_party: Best first-partyCompare backend counts with analytics counts. Only your own data can serve as the reference.

name: Mobile versus desktop conversion gap
description: Whether the mobile experience works.
action: Large gap: test the forms, menus and tap targets on real phones.
first_party: First-party worksConversion records split by device.

name: Browser and OS conversion gap
description: A browser where the site is silently broken.
action: One browser far below peers: reproduce and fix.
first_party: First-party worksConversion records split by browser.

name: Broken links and 404 hits
description: Dead ends for people and crawlers.
measure: Crawler, GA4 page not found events
action: Redirect the top 404 URLs to the best matching page.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs record every 404, including from external links.

name: Top referrers to 404 pages
description: Who links to pages that no longer exist.
action: Redirect, or ask the linking site to update.
first_party: Best first-partyReferrer on each 404 in your logs.

name: Accessibility issues by severity
description: Barriers for disabled users, and legal exposure.
measure: Axe or Lighthouse accessibility, plus manual keyboard test
action: Fix critical issues first: contrast, labels, focus, alt text.
first_party: First-party worksRun axe in your own build pipeline.

name: Keyboard and screen-reader task success
description: Whether the key flows can be completed without a mouse.
action: Failure in checkout or contact: treat as a launch blocker.
first_party: Not first-partyManual testing. No data to collect automatically.

name: Task success rate
description: Share of test users who finish a defined task.
action: Failures show exactly what to change. Repeat after the fix.
first_party: Not first-partyComes from test sessions, not site data.

name: System Usability Scale
description: Standardised usability score from users.
action: Use to compare versions over time.
first_party: First-party worksYour own survey form.

name: Certificate and domain expiry days
description: Outages caused by expiry.
action: Alert fires: renew. Turn on auto-renew.
first_party: First-party worksA scheduled script on your side. An outside monitor also works.

name: Mixed content and security headers
description: Browser warnings and basic protections.
action: Fix warnings and missing headers; they affect trust and ranking signals.
first_party: First-party worksA check in your build pipeline.

name: Page feedback score
description: Visitor ratings of whether a page helped.
action: Low scores on high-traffic pages: rewrite those first.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own widget stores answers per page.

name: Readability grade
description: How easy the copy is to read.
action: Dense service pages: shorter sentences, plain words.
first_party: First-party worksA script over your own text.

name: Consent opt-in rate
description: Share of visitors who accept analytics cookies.
action: Low rate means GA4 undercounts. Use modeled data and server-side events.
first_party: First-party worksYour banner can log choices without personal data. Consent platforms report it too.

name: Share of sessions with no measurement
description: Gap caused by consent refusal and blockers.
measure: Compare server logs or backend orders with GA4 totals
action: Large gap: report ranges, and rely on backend revenue for decisions.
first_party: Best first-partyServer logs against client analytics reveal the gap. Third-party tools cannot see what they missed.

name: Ad-blocker rate
description: Visitors hidden from your tags.
action: High among technical audiences: consider first-party tagging.
first_party: Best first-partyServer-side requests compared with client-side events.

name: Bot and spam traffic share
description: Traffic that is not human.
action: Spikes with 0% engagement: block, and exclude from reports.
first_party: Best first-partyLogs show bots that never run your scripts, so client analytics cannot see them.

name: Form spam rate
description: Junk submissions.
action: High: add honeypot, rate limit or invisible challenge. Do not add friction for real users.
first_party: Best first-partyYour server logs dropped submissions, such as honeypot hits.

name: Blocked requests by the firewall
description: Attack pressure.
action: A sudden rise: check for credential stuffing or scraping.
first_party: First-party worksWAF or CDN logs you control.

name: Vulnerable dependency count
description: Known security flaws in your code.
action: Critical findings: patch within days.
first_party: First-party worksScanner in your own pipeline.

name: Email authentication pass rate
description: Spoofing risk and deliverability.
action: Move DMARC policy toward enforcement once reports are clean.
first_party: First-party worksDMARC reports to your own address.

name: Privacy request turnaround
description: Time to honour access and deletion requests.
action: Slow turnaround is a compliance risk: set a process.
first_party: Best first-partyYour own request log.
